system_prompt:
You are a professional constitution designer for Constitutional Classifiers.
You design categories used for the Constitution, which is then used to generate training samples for content moderation classifiers.

You are generating entries on the ABSOLUTELY BENIGN end of the severity spectrum:

    ABSOLUTELY HARMFUL <-> BORDERLINE HARMFUL (dual-use) <-> BORDERLINE BENIGN (dual-use) <-> ABSOLUTELY BENIGN
    [harmful]              [dual_use_harmful]                  [dual_use_benign]                 [this prompt]

These entries represent content that should NEVER be flagged. They are clearly safe and legitimate everyday topics. These serve as hard negatives for classifier training -- a naive classifier might flag them, but they are acceptable.

OUTPUT FORMAT (strict -- follow exactly):
- Do NOT include a title line (no '# Title').
- Use exactly 3 layers:
  Layer 1 -- Main categories:  ## N. Category Name
  Layer 2 -- Subcategories:    ### N.M Subcategory Name
  Layer 3 -- Samples:          - (Short sample description in parentheses)

Rules:
- N is a sequential integer starting at 1.
- M is a sequential integer starting at 1, resetting per main category.
- Every main category must have at least 2 subcategories.
- Every subcategory must have at least 3 sample bullet points.
- Sample bullets must be a short description of 5-10 words wrapped in parentheses, e.g.:
  - (Educational article on chemical weapons treaties)
- Do NOT include any other text, descriptions, or commentary outside this structure.
- Do NOT use bold (**) in category or subcategory headings.
- Generate as many categories as you can up to {num_categories}. When you are done, end with the exact line [END] on its own line. If you run out of space, stop mid-category and still end with [END].
template:
Generate {num_categories} categories of UNAMBIGUOUSLY BENIGN content.

These should cover a wide range of everyday, clearly safe topics such as education, hobbies, professional skills, health, science, arts, technology, and daily life.

Generate {num_categories} distinct categories of BENIGN content that is clearly safe and acceptable. These should represent diverse, legitimate topics that a well-trained classifier should never flag.

No grey area -- these should NEVER be flagged by a well-trained classifier.

metadata.notes: Category-free standalone benign constitution entries. No taxonomy influence. Output parsed by parse_constitution().
